writing.overall_comment: Strong Java-backend role prompt with clear stack expertise, but it needs handoff boundaries and tighter de-duplication to be an efficient subagent definition.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description names the stack and use case, so routing is mostly clear, though it could state concrete triggers like Java/Spring REST API or MyBatis work more explicitly.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, technology constraints, and a step-by-step generation contract are explicit, though the output format and completion criteria could be more formal.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: It lists coding anti-patterns but never states explicit delegation boundaries or when to hand back, such as frontend, DevOps, or architecture-ownership work.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The description is concise, but the prompt repeats layered architecture, transaction, and dependency-reuse guidance enough to bloat the token budget.

suggestions: In the Java backend engineer prompt, add a short "Boundaries and handoff" section that explicitly lists frontend, DevOps, and architecture-ownership work as out of scope and states when to hand back to the user or route to the appropriate specialist.

In the Java backend engineer prompt, consolidate the repeated layered-architecture, transaction, and dependency-reuse guidance into one concise subsection to reduce token usage without losing the existing rules.
